scope: Selected development queries; reviewed source targets, not exhaustive repository answers.

review.method: Independent AI source review, sealed before author proposal adjudication.
limitations: Sealing records the review process but does not prove perfect blindness.

Q02.interpretation: Locate the actual finalized-header execution-timestamp read and its local response/type chain. Do not infer external API time units or bug correctness.
conditions: Include the actual Voyager query_latest_timestamp read and response/type chain.
Interpret all time-unit evidence as local source usage only; external API correctness is outside this diagnostic.

Q03.interpretation: Locate TextColumn time formatting, trait binding, date delegation and default time format. Timezone resolution, formatter execution and rendering are conditional expanded context.
conditions: Binding, time-to-date delegation and the default format are complementary source targets.
Include timezone, formatter execution or rendering evidence only when that additional behavior is requested.

Q04.interpretation: Locate the Hubble Aptos consumer, its imported type identity and local microseconds-to-nanoseconds conversion. Do not infer Movement behavior or all Aptos API specifications.
conditions: Include the Aptos Block import to establish local type identity.
Interpret microseconds as the local Hubble consumer assumption; no external API specification claim.

Q05.interpretation: Locate the Rust ConsensusState declaration in the Ethereum crate. ABI and protobuf representations apply only when those representations are requested; readers, writers and import chains are conditional context.
conditions: Match the Ethereum crate semantic identity, not a required literal EthereumConsensusState identifier.
ABI or protobuf definitions are conditional representation alternatives; do not count them as additional mandatory Rust declaration targets.

Q07.interpretation: Column-group definition order and the creation chain for a new physical compressed chunk.
conditions: Applies to newly created physical compressed chunks in the pinned commit; existing relation reuse, historical layouts and post-ALTER layouts are outside this diagnostic.
Detailed within-group metadata order is conditional expanded context, retained in the review ledger rather than made mandatory.
The decoded second phrase is a nonvoting creation-chain variant, not another independent question.
The internal compressed hypertable root starts with an empty schema; that alternative interpretation is recorded but is outside the selected physical-chunk scope.

query_origin.tool_input: ["compressed table schema creation column order", "create compressed chunk relation columns"]
query_origin.transformation: Decode the JSON-shaped string and select its first phrase.

Q09.interpretation: Exact lookup of the ordinary Rust ExecutionPayload.timestamp declaration; reported separately from semantic questions.
conditions: Requires the exact ordinary Rust type identity and timestamp field; it does not ask for a time-unit specification.
SSZ and light-client Header alternatives apply only to expanded interpretations and remain in the review ledger; they are not silent substitutes for this exact-name control.
This lookup control uses the unchanged scorer and is excluded from semantic quality means.

E01.interpretation: Locate the Elasticsearch ListenableFuture implementation when a listener is registered after success or failure has already completed.
conditions: The four targets cover type identity, entry and completed fast path, terminal dispatch, and actual success and failure callback delivery.
Both spans in each entry/fast-path or callback-delivery evidence set are required; finding only the success branch is insufficient.
Concurrent completion retries, executor/context wrappers, documentation and tests are supplementary for this implementation query, not substitutes for the minimum implementation chain.
The plain query is an explicitly selected mechanical decoding of the recorded one-element JSON-array-shaped string. Historical backend normalization and equivalence of the two forms remain unknown.

query_origin.transformation: Decode the single element of the JSON-shaped string; use it as one derived diagnostic query.
